To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the digestibility of P in pigs increases as they grow from 30 to >60 kg BW and then remains stable until 100 to 120 kg BW.
in pigs the efficacy of As. niger phytases in rendering phytatic P available depends on the physiological status of pigs, with the lowest efficacy in lactating sows.

the efficacy of A. niger phytases in rendering phytatic P digestible in pigs depends on the physiological status of pigs and that the amount of A. nigger phytase to add to diets should be tailored to target categories of pigs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of feed additives that can be used for the formulation of diets for all stages of the life cycle of pigs.
the efficacy of As. niger phytases in rendering P available for absorption in different categories of pigs.
the effect of phytase supplementation of swine diets on P and Ca utilization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the efficacy of As. niger phytases is influenced by the pig physiological status.
the efficacy of As. niger phytases in generating digestible phosphorus is not influenced by the physiological status of pigs.
the efficacy of As. niger phytases to render phytate phosphorous available in the gastrointestinal tract of pigs is influenced by the physiological status of the pigs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the efficacy of A. niger phytases is influenced by the physiological state of pigs and is lower during lactation than during growth or pregnancy.
phytase supplementation is more effective in growing-finishing pigs than in sows, and in piglets than in sows at the beginning or end of pregnancy.

the amount of phytic P that can be rendered digestible by Aspergillus phytase depends on the physiological status of pigs and is in the order of 30 to 70 g digestible phytate P for 1 kg diet in piglets and growing pigs, respectively, and of 30 to.40 g digestible phytic P for 1kg diet in sows.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the efficacy of the phytic acid-degrading phytase in swine diets is not only influenced by feedstuff composition, as is generally assumed, but is also influenced by the physiological status of pigs, which in turn is related to their age and reproductive stage.
the efficiency of P utilization in pigs increases with BW and that the efficacy of As. niger phytases to generate digestible P decreases with increasing physiological age of pigs.
in the formulation and feeding of diets for lactating sows and growing-finishing swine, the amount of added phytase should be at least 1,000 and 500 FTU per kilogram, respectively.
